news_title: Product safety recall – Fidlock Hermetic dry bag - The National Consumer Commission (NCC)
efet_title: Product safety recall - Fidlock Hermetic dry bag - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recall – Fidlock Hermetic dry bag
Date Posted:
September 11, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) informs consumers about the recall of certain Fidlock Hermetic dry bag Medi products in the
petrol colourway,
as notified by the manufacturer, Fidlock GmbH. The affected product can be identified by Article number D-11111A-F0000 (PTTT) and Lot number 2409140930201. The lot number is located on the back of the seal strip.
According to Fidlock GmbH, the recall is due to a defect in the adhesive bonding of the closure strips to the bag’s film. The closure strips may partially or completely detach, which can cause individual magnets to fall out.The magnets, which are classified as small parts, may pose a serious health risk if swallowed, particularly by children, resulting in serious internal injuries and may be life-threatening. Fifty units were sold in South Africa through Orka Paddles from 4 December 2024 to 1 September 2026.
Consumers who have purchased the affected product are advised to stop using it immediately and keep it out of the reach of children. Consumers should take a photograph of the entire product and the lot number for documentation purposes and contact the seller to arrange a replacement of the product or a full refund.
Questions relating to this recall may be directed to:
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.

news_title: What you need to know about Isuzu's massive recall of D-Max bakkies - EWN
efet_title: Product safety recall - Isuzu RG19 motor vehicles - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recall – Isuzu RG19 motor vehicles
Date Posted:
September 8, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) notify consumers of a product safety recall issued by Isuzu Motors South Africa (Pty) Ltd (Isuzu). The recall affects two thousand five hundred and eighty-six (2 586) Isuzu RG19 (Field Action 26FSL0080) bakkies. These are single cabs, double cabs and extended bakkies and were sold nationwide between 11May 2026 and 3 July 2026. The vehicles were also exported to Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, eSwatini, Uganda and Zambia.
According to the supplier, there is a possibility that the brake pedal pivot pin may be loose. In this case, the brake pedal may move laterally (sideways) during brake application. This may make it more difficult for the driver to fully depress the brake pedal and could potentially reduce braking performance when attempting to stop the vehicle.
Consumers should present their vehicles to the nearest Isuzu Dealership for an inspection and replacement of the defective component. Any remedial work will be carried out at no cost to the consumer.
“A vehicle’s braking system is a critical safety component of a vehicle. It is therefore imperative for owners or users of these vehicles to contact their preferred authorised dealership without any delay,” said Acting Commissioner Hardin Ratshisusu.
Questions relating to this recall may be directed to:
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.

efet_title: PRODUCT RECALL: 50ML SINGLE-USE NEUTRALIZING SHAMPOO CONTAINEDIN DARK AND LOVELY MOISTURE-PLUS KITS
efet_body:
Product Recall: 50ml Single-Use Neutralizing Shampoo Contained in Dark and Lovely Moisture-Plus Kits
Date Posted:
June 10, 2024
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) advises anyone with 50ml single-use neutralizing shampoo found in Dark and Lovely Moisture Plus Kits (Regular and Super) or Dark and Lovely Anti Breakage Kits to stop using the product immediately and return it to the place of purchase for a full refund.
